# dsh-dwf

Dynamic workflows for **DeepSeek Harness** — a workflow engine that replaces the
official `workflowE
ngine` slot with a compiled, replayable, resumable one.

`dsh-dwf` brings the ZCode-style workflow contract to DSH: a **TypeScript-checked
script facade** in

stead of plain JS, a **replay journal** in SQLite, a
**deterministic guest sandbox**, persistent **a

ctor subagents**, and a
**model pool** that spreads load across providers and fails over on quota er

subagents**, and a
**model pool** that spreads load across providers and fails over on quota errors.

## What you get
| Capability | Detail |
| Typed workflow scripts | `agent<T>()` results are validated against a JSON Schema generated from a

script-local TS interface — the facade is checked at compile time |
| Replay journal | Every run, e
vent, node and actor is persisted in SQLite (`dwf_run` / `dwf_event` / `dwf_node` / `dwf_actor`); th

e model tool reads the same database the engine writes |
| Deterministic guest | Scripts run in a re
stricted realm: no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no filesystem, no network — a run can be replay

ed |
| Persistent actors | One `agent()` handle keeps its conversation across asks (FIFO per actor)

|
| Model pool | Unbound actors spread across providers (`spread` or `round-robin`); deterministic p

rovider failures cool down and fail over |
| Stall detection | A deadlocked or stalled script settle

s as a clean error instead of hanging the run |
| Background runs | `run_in_background` via the host

ror instead of hanging the run |
| Background runs | `run_in_background` via the host job registry |
## Requirements

- **Node.js ≥ 22.6** (the package ships TypeScript sources and relies on native
type stripping; deve

loped and tested on Node 24)
- **DSH 0.2.1-rc.3** (pinned; the engine implements the `workflowEngine

` seam of
that release)
## Install

`dsh-dwf` resolves its `@deepseek-ai/*` imports from the DSH host, so it must be
installed **into a

DSH profile** — not into a bare project (a plain `npm i`
outside DSH leaves the peer packages unreso

`dwf-engine` (publishes the

`workflowEngine` service) and `dwf` (registers the
`dwf` model tool). Both must point at the **same*

* `dbPath` — that database is
the single source of truth shared by engine and tool.

## Writing a workflow

The model calls the `dwf` tool with a script. Scripts are TypeScript bodies with
top-level `await` a
nd a final `return`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Facade: `agent` / `ask<T>` / `model` / `phase` / `log` / `report` /
`publishArtifact` / `channel` /

`future` / `world` (`run`, `read`) /
`files` (`glob`, `read`, `grep`) / `git` (`changedFiles`, `diff

`, `status`,
`log`) / `args` / `hole`.
## Verification status

Verified on Windows + Node 24.20.0 against DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 in a `personal`
profile, with a real host
boot and journal reconciliation:

- typecheck, stall/unit/integration suites and the no-host smoke suite: green
- real-machine smoke:

report-then-return script completes (no false stall);
an actor round-trip returns a real model reply

- `dsh-workflow-gate` coexistence: the gate's verdict equals the command exit
code, no model involv

`dsh-workflow-gate` coexistence: the gate's verdict equals the command exit
code, no model involved
Known boundaries (deliberate deferrals, not bugs):

- workflow-script `amend`/resume caching and `SaveWorkflow` are placeholders
- artifact presets (cha

rt/table/metrics/board) are placeholders; `report` items
and artifact rows are recorded in the journ

al instead
- the host exposes no confirmation-surface, artifact-card or completion-
notification API

at this DSH version, so phase/command preview and artifact
cards are not wired
- `hole()` answers w

ith a deterministic "unavailable" error rather than parking
the run
